handout_heading: Gastritis classification and causes of gastropathy
handout_text:
Gastritis can be classified by acuity (acute vs chronic), by its histological features, or by etiology.
Gastropathy (epithelial injury and regeneration without inflammation) is usually caused by bile reflux, hypovolaemia, or chronic congestion as in portal hypertension (portal hypertensive gastropathy).
In practice the two overlap: gastritis may show mucosal injury, and gastropathy may show some inflammatory reaction.

Over time chronic gastritis raises the risk of gastric ulcers, upper GI bleeding and certain gastric neoplasms.

In alcoholics and chronic NSAID users the chronic gastritis may be completely asymptomatic.
